brief.subject: Final auto-enrollment rules, W-9 errors and SBA rule changes
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Retirement Plan Auto-Enrollment Rules; SBA Revises Two Programs
brief.dek: Final SECURE 2.0 auto-enrollment regulations arrive, unchecked W-9s can become 1099 headaches, and SBA updates two programs.
brief.lede: The IRS has issued final regulations on the automatic enrollment requirements under Section 414A. Employers that sponsor certain retirement plans should review how the rules apply to them.

sections.heading: Auto-Enrollment Rules Are Now Final
bullets: Final IRS regulations now govern the automatic enrollment requirements under Section 414A for certain retirement plans.
The rules carry out changes made by the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022.
Certain cash or deferred arrangements must qualify as eligible automatic contribution arrangements that meet additional requirements.
Employers that maintain affected plans, along with participants and beneficiaries, fall within the rules' scope.

sections.heading: Unchecked W-9s Can Trigger IRS Notices
bullets: A W-9 can be collected on time and filed properly yet still contain a mismatched name and TIN.
That bad pairing can carry over onto a Form 1099 issued to the vendor.
The result can be an IRS notice months later, so verifying vendor details before 1099 filing saves cleanup work.

sections.heading: SBA Streamlines Surety Bond Guarantees
bullets: A final SBA rule reduces document submission and retention burdens for surety companies in the Surety Bond Guarantee program.
The rule fixes conflicting provisions in the program regulations.
It also revises outdated Preferred Surety admission requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.

sections.heading: More Leverage for SBIC Funds
bullets: An SBA interim final rule implements the Investing in All of America Act of 2025 for the SBIC program.
It raises the maximum leverage available to SBICs issuing standard debentures, at ratios of up to two-to-one against private capital.

brief.seo_description: IRS finalizes Section 414A auto-enrollment rules, W-9 name and TIN errors can lead to 1099 notices, and SBA updates surety bond and SBIC programs.

items.title: The W-9 Problem Your Busy Season Workflow Audit Can Miss
items.snippet: A vendor's Form W-9 can be collected on time, filed correctly, and still create work months later. If nobody checks the name and TIN, an incorrect combination can flow into a Form 1099 and eventually trigger an IRS notice.

items.title: Winning the First-Year Client: How Tax Firms Reach New Homeowners Before Tax Season
items.snippet: Many new homeowners will choose a tax professional during their first year in the home. The only question is whether they choose your firm or the one across town.

items.title: The Insurance Gap Inside a Tax Firm’s WISP
items.snippet: A written information security plan can meet an important compliance duty and still leave a firm exposed if its cyber application, control evidence, and incident response steps tell a different story.

items.title: Many AI-Adopting Clients Would Use AI to Fact-Check Their Accountant’s Work, TaxDome Report Says
items.snippet: A new report from practice management platform TaxDome reveals that 74% of clients who use artificial intelligence have either fact-checked or would consider fact-checking their accountant's work with AI.

items.snippet: Publication of the tier 2 tax rates for calendar year 2027 as required by section 3241(d) of the Internal Revenue Code. Tier 2 taxes on railroad employees, employers, and employee representatives are one source of funding for benefits under the Railroad Retirement Act.

items.title: Rule: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
items.snippet: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.
